cards.q: What is redistribution and what is the critical catch when moving OSPF routes into EIGRP?
cards.a: Redistribution injects routes from one routing domain into another at a boundary router (ASBR / redistribution point). The critical catch is that EIGRP requires a seed metric: OSPF cost does not map to the EIGRP composite metric, so without a seed metric the routes are not advertised.

cards.q: What are the five values in an EIGRP seed metric, and in what order are they given?
cards.a: Bandwidth (kbps), delay (microseconds/10), reliability, load, and MTU. Example: metric 1000 100 255 1 1500.

cards.q: Under redistribute ospf, which route sources are redistributed by default versus only with a keyword?
cards.a: OSPF routes are redistributed (excluding own subnet/max) with the keyword. Static routes need 'redistribute static', connected routes need 'redistribute connected', and the default route only appears with include-connected or default-information.

cards.q: When OSPF routes are redistributed into EIGRP, what kind of EIGRP routes do OSPF external type 1/2 and internal routes become?
cards.a: They all propagate as EIGRP external routes.

cards.q: How does the OSPF metric map to the EIGRP metric when redistributing OSPF into EIGRP?
cards.a: It does not map: the OSPF cost is meaningless inside EIGRP, and the boundary router must assign a seed metric for the redistributed routes.

cards.q: How can a route-map be used to selectively redistribute OSPF into EIGRP?
cards.a: A route-map matches prefixes with 'match ip address prefix-list' and sets the seed metric with 'set metric 10000 100 255 1 1500', then the route-map is applied to the redistribute ospf command. Matched prefixes get the seed metric while others are dropped.

cards.q: What must be configured for bidirectional (two-way) OSPF-to-EIGRP redistribution?
cards.a: Both directions must be independently seeded: OSPF uses 'redistribute eigrp 100 subnets metric-type 1' and EIGRP uses 'redistribute ospf 1 metric 10000 100 255 1 1500'. Missing one side breaks reachability, and OSPF needs the 'subnets' keyword to redistribute non-classful prefixes.

cards.q: What are the key redistribution design rules for OSPF-to-EIGRP?
cards.a: Use one boundary router for cleanliness, always seed metrics or routes vanish, filter at both edges to prevent feedback loops, and set route tags to mark origin for later policy.

cards.q: Which command shows EIGRP redistribution and route-map filter behavior along with the routes?
cards.a: 'show ip protocols' shows redistribution and filters; 'show ip eigrp topology', 'show ip ospf database', and 'show ip route' are used to verify redistributed routes.

cards.q: No EIGRP routes appear for a redistributed OSPF domain. What is the most likely cause and check?
cards.a: A missing seed metric is the likely cause; check with 'show ip eigrp topology'. Route-map mismatches, a missing 'subnets' keyword, or wrong default-metric values are other causes.

cards.q: What does EIGRP do if you try to redistribute OSPF routes without a seed metric?
cards.a: EIGRP refuses the redistributed routes — they are not advertised at all.

cards.q: When OSPF is redistributed into EIGRP, what is the resulting route type and source in EIGRP?
cards.a: The OSPF routes become EIGRP external routes (the source of route is external).

cards.q: What does the 'subnets' keyword do in OSPF redistribution?
cards.a: It allows non-classful prefixes to be redistributed; without it, only classful routes are redistributed.

cards.q: If you configure OSPF-to-EIGRP redistribution in only one direction on one router, what happens?
cards.a: Reachability is only one-way: one-directional configuration on one router gives one-way reachability unless the reverse direction is also configured.
